headline: V26-3694: give lanes and leads commands for what they do by hand today

V26-3643.title: Keep the merge queue's sync merges off a lane's branch, so a lane can push its own base merge

criteria.text: After the queue stops a synced candidate, a lane can push an authorized base merge of its reviewed head and hand off, with no one running a raw force-push.
Nothing a lane or lead wrote is ever dropped: only the queue's own sync commits are moved off the lane's branch, or never placed there.
The move, where one happens, is in the journal with its reason.
After a failed run, the lane can push a fix on top of its handed head without a force push.
Where the queue does leave a commit on the story branch, the candidate.stopped entry names it.

V26-3649.title: Pin the outside-span laneOutside item's detail

criteria.text: The outside-span and whole-file laneOutside items' fields.detail is pinned to its text, for example "It changed line 2, outside its span."

V26-3640.title: Grant line spans by anchor, and treat an edit at a span's edge as the span's

criteria.text: c1: A span granted by anchor resolves to the right lines and records the coordinates.
c2: Replacing a span's last line with that line plus new lines is accepted.
c3: An insertion just past a span is refused when another lane owns the next line.
c4: A span a base edit crossed without touching its lines is carried forward by one command, journalled.

V26-3432.title: Offer lead-assign's co-change warnings as owns candidates

criteria.text: A co-change file lead-assign warns about can be added to the lane's owns without hand-editing the delivery file.
A one-line pin update in an unowned file can be accepted with a recorded reason.

V26-3434.title: Let the lead patch a lane row without racing the queue's version

criteria.text: A lead patch to a lane row succeeds while the queue writes other parts of the record, and still refuses when the same row changed.
Patching status on a lane row is refused with a message naming state.

V26-3578.title: Keep a delivery's record out of its own story's lane checkout when the two share a key

criteria.text: c1: A delivery whose key equals a story key runs with its record somewhere lane-start doesn't use, with no extra step.
c2: doctor --delivery reports the collision.

V26-3628.title: Let the lead add a lane to a running delivery with one command

criteria.text: c1: A lead adds a lane to a running delivery with one command. The lane is then in the delivery file and in the record, and lead-own and lead-assign accept it.
c2: Initial claims that overlap another lane's claims, a shared output, or a region claim are refused, and nothing is written.
c3: lead-plan change --kind added can add a story on a lane added that way, with no hand edit to the delivery file or the record.
c4: No step needs the state tool's raw patch on laneOwnership.

V26-3676.title: Don't tell a lane session to start the lead's lead-wait

criteria.text: The hook tells which session is the lead's from something other than the checkout the last command ran in, and never asks a lane session to start lead-wait.
A test in the hooks module covers a lane session that ran a command from the lead checkout.

V26-3427.title: Keep lanes waiting on their own lens results inside a turn

criteria.text: A lane running a review round ends no turn between review-prepare and review-reduce unless it is blocked or has a question: review-wait waits on its lens results in the foreground, and review-prepare and the lane brief name it.

finish.label: The stories
finish.text: V26-3643, V26-3649, V26-3640, V26-3432, V26-3434, V26-3578, V26-3628, V26-3676 and V26-3427 land on integrate/lane-commands through its merge queue

finish.label: Local suite
finish.text: The full local suite passes on macOS with Python 3.11 at the integration head, with --workers 4 --budget tests/suite-budget.json

finish.label: Into main
finish.text: The integration base is reviewed for main, as the orchestrate-work guide's integration review says, and merged into main

outcome.summary: Lanes and leads do with commands what they do by hand today.
outcome.text: Lanes and leads do with commands what they do by hand today. The queue never leaves its own commits on a lane's branch; a lead grants, carries and accepts ownership with commands and adds a lane to a running delivery in one write; a lead patches a lane row while the queue writes the rest of the record; a delivery whose key is also a story's key sets up with no extra step; the stop hook tells a lane from the lead by the session; and a lane waits on its lenses in the foreground.
